author: Nayan Seth,Han Li
description:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday hinted at sanctioning Chinese banks over their commercial links with Iran, just weeks before Chinese leader Xi Jinping is expected to visit Washington for a bilateral summit.
“Who said I’m not?” Trump said in response to a reporter’s question about why the US had not sanctioned Chinese banks for their dealings with Iranian entities.
“Well, I don’t have to announce everything, do I?”
Trump’s remarks come days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced...
title: Trump hints at sanctions on Chinese banks over Iran ties before Xi’s expected US visit

author: Vincent Chow
description:
The United States should take a leaf out of Beijing’s industrial playbook and strategically open up specific sectors to Chinese investment while ensuring that technology transfers occur, US industrial policy and supply chain experts said at an event on Thursday.
The assessment comes as Washington mulls new broad restrictions on Chinese technology, including a proposed prohibition on the sale of cars with connected-vehicle technology linked to China and a ban on imports of Chinese humanoid robots...
title: US urged to use Beijing playbook to secure Chinese tech transfers

author: Nayan Seth,Dewey Sim,Khushboo Razdan
description:
Chinese and US officials are discussing whether business leaders will join President Xi Jinping’s delegation to the United States next month, as the two sides prepare to extend a one-year trade agreement reached in Busan last October, according to people familiar with the talks.
The negotiations come as Xi is expected to meet US President Donald Trump in Washington on September 24. Trump travelled to Beijing in May with a large group of top American CEOs, including the heads of Tesla, Apple,...
title: Chinese executives may join Xi’s US trip, as trade truce extension ‘almost certain’

author: Richard Heydarian
description:
In arguably his most important foreign trip, Elbridge Colby, US undersecretary for defence policy, visited key Southeast Asian capitals this month. In a speech in Manila, the Pentagon policy chief extolled America’s “flexible realism”, which he said serves “the practical, concrete interests of regular Americans” and echoes Southeast Asian nations’ commitment to “pragmatism, an openness to dialogue, respect for counterparts, proud nationalism, and a focus on economic prosperity”.
Amid the United...
title: Why Southeast Asia isn’t buying the US’ offer of ‘flexible realism’

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazil will not be able to make rare earth magnets from its own raw materials before 2032, the coordinator of the country’s main magnet pilot plant said on Wednesday, leaving China’s near monopoly on the technology intact for years to come.
Andre Luis Pimenta de Faria, who runs the plant for Senai, the research and training arm of Brazil’s national industry confederation, told a public policy panel at Exposibram, the country’s largest mining congress, that first batches could come by the end of...
title: Brazil’s rare earths will not loosen China’s magnet grip this decade, researchers say

author: Dannie Peng
description:
While extreme weather is disrupting nuclear power generation in some parts of the world, it is unlikely to derail China’s rapid expansion in the sector, according to an industry specialist.
The unusually hot and dry summer has disrupted reactors across Europe, forcing units to shut down from France to Romania, as river levels have fallen and water temperatures risen.
France – where nuclear accounts for around 70 per cent of electricity generation – had a record shortfall of more than 20 per cent...
title: Why climate extremes will not stop expansion of China’s nuclear power industry

author: Carol Yang
description:
Asian-American lawmakers in the US Congress have condemned a right-wing podcast that called for the forced internment of Chinese-Americans during a hypothetical war with Beijing, warning that such rhetoric fuelled hate against the community.
The joint statement was released by congresswomen Grace Meng, chairwoman of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (Capac), and Judy Chu, Capac’s chairwoman emerita, as well as congressman Ted Lieu, vice-chairman of the House Democratic Caucus.
The...
title: US lawmakers condemn right-wing podcast’s calls for Chinese-American internment

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Chinese scientists have developed a cross-border early warning system with counterparts in Nepal to monitor Himalayan glacial lake outburst floods. The system has issued timely alerts over the past several years, effectively preventing casualties.
But on Wednesday, a high-altitude ice-rock avalanche took everyone by surprise. The debris flow hit a river in Nepal, generating a devastating flash flood that swept all the way down to Gyirong county in the Tibet autonomous region in China.
Some...
title: China and Nepal built an early warning system for melting glaciers in Himalayas. Does it work?

author: Alyssa Chen,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The catastrophic flash floods and mudslide that devastated the Gyirong Port crossing along the China-Nepal border on Wednesday have dealt a heavy blow to China-Nepal trade and imperilled Kathmandu’s push to cut reliance on Indian transit routes.
However, if Beijing and Kathmandu are to proceed with ambitious infrastructure projects, they are expected to take environmental factors into consideration and adjust their construction methods accordingly, one expert said.


Chinese officials confirmed...
title: Himalayan glacier collapse hits crucial China-Nepal trade route as casualties mount

author: Caroline Lin
description:
The coastal Chinese province of Zhejiang is battening down for the approach of Typhoon Saudel, with flights cancelled across the area.
The eastern province is home to a number of major commercial centres, including the industrial hub of Ningbo, the port city of Zhoushan, and Wenzhou.
Ningbo Lishe International Airport said flights in and out of the facility would be suspended from 11.30pm on Thursday. In Wenzhou, 90 flights were cancelled, while 22 flights were grounded in Zhoushan.
According to...
title: Flights, ferries cancelled in Shanghai and Shenzhen as Typhoon Saudel closes in

author: Neil Denslow,Raymond Ma
description:
Bill Gates is likely to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping later this year as the Microsoft co-founder seeks to rally support for global cooperation on artificial intelligence (AI) risks.
A meeting may take place in November, Reuters reported on Wednesday citing a Gates spokesman. Xi last met his “old friend” in 2023, when Gates became the first foreign business leader to visit the Chinese president following the Covid-19 pandemic.
Gates also published a 6,000-word essay on Wednesday that called...
title: Gates pitches US-China AI cooperation ahead of Xi meeting

author: Shaoshan Liu
description:
The next big competition in artificial intelligence is over science. The question is shifting from who has the largest model to who can use AI to shorten the discovery cycle: forming a hypothesis, running simulations, designing an experiment, operating equipment, collecting results and learning from them.
The United States made that shift explicit. The Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission aims to bring together 17 national laboratories into an integrated discovery platform to double the...
title: How Shenzhen can win the ‘AI for science’ race

author: Orange Wang
description:
China should forge a national consensus on “regaining mastery of the oceans” and direct overseas investment returns into defence spending to brace for sea-power competition with the US, according to a prominent Chinese academic.
Di Dongsheng, associate dean of Renmin University’s school of international studies in Beijing, warned on Tuesday that as economic ties between the United States, the dominant maritime power, and China, which relies heavily on sea-bound trade, shifted towards...
title: What China can do to secure trade routes in its coming high-seas struggle with US

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has urged Washington to help “remove interference and overcome obstacles” to high-level exchanges as the two sides prepare for President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the US next month.
Meeting US Ambassador David Perdue in Beijing on Wednesday, Wang said both sides should put the Xi-Trump consensus into practice, focus on a positive agenda and manage differences to keep ties “stable, healthy and sustainable”, according to China’s foreign ministry.
In a social...
title: Wang Yi calls on US to ‘overcome obstacles’ ahead of Xi-Trump meeting

author: Shi Huang
description:
Beijing’s hundreds of thousands of weeping willows and poplars have been a welcome source of shelter from the fierce summer sun for more than four decades – but they may also be an unexpected source of pollution, according to new research.
Scientists warned that this urban greenery may be “choking” the Chinese capital’s 20 million residents by increasing the levels of ozone in the city’s air.
Smog caused by the ozone released by car exhausts has been recognised as a public health problem since...
title: Chinese scientists discover that trees are producing ozone smog in Beijing

author: William Zheng,Yuanyue Dang
description: For more, check out the South China Morning Post’s full anti-corruption data bank project:
title: China’s anti-corruption drive by the numbers

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Tokyo is experimenting with a radically faster way of buying new weapons – picking a domestically built interceptor drone less than three months after launching the procurement process.
Analysts say this shift could help Japan respond more quickly to China’s expanding military capabilities.
The defence ministry’s Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA) announced on Tuesday that it had signed a contract to buy Terra Drone’s Terra B1 system following competitive trials.
The decision...
title: Japan fast-tracks anti-drone system amid China’s military build-up
Global US immigrant visa pause: the fallout across China, Asia and Hong Kong

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
A massive mudslide and flash flood struck the Gyirong Port area along the China-Nepal border on Wednesday, leaving at least 160 people dead and more than 1,000 missing across both sides of the divide.
According to the latest official update from the Shigatse municipal government press conference on Thursday morning, three people have been confirmed dead and 558 remain missing on the Chinese side.


Two survivors have been rescued. Earlier figures of 265 missing were revised upwards as search...
title: China-Nepal border disaster: 1,000-plus missing as Beijing sends rescue teams

author: Victoria Bela
description:
China has launched the world’s first 100-kilowatt (kW) floating solar farm built with bamboo frames, offering a more environmentally friendly approach to offshore energy.
The floating solar platform, named Jilin-2, is made of composite bamboo tubes and pipes. It has been deployed at a demonstration base off the coast of Yantai in the eastern province of Shandong.
It will supply power to an integrated hydrogen, ammonia and methanol production project, manufacturer Yantai CIMC Raffles Ocean...
title: China launches world’s first 100kW bamboo-built floating solar farm off Shandong coast
